concepts.proposed_markdown: A separate ASC 606 guide maps the standard's five steps—contract identification, performance-obligation identification, transaction-price determination, allocation, and recognition—to Metronome contracts, products, pricing, usage, invoices, balances, ledgers, exports, and integration identifiers. Metronome describes daily and product-level data, billed-versus-earned views, true-up linkage, and external ERP or revenue-subledger integration as support for merchant-owned workflows. The same guide expressly says Metronome is not a revenue-recognition platform, does not generate journal entries or make accounting determinations, and leaves policy and compliance to the customer. Its broad full-history, immutable-audit-trail, schema-stability, real-time, retention, and audit-ready claims do not replace table-specific export grain, cadence, duplicate-delivery, snapshot, correction, reconciliation, or sign-off authority. [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]]
warnings: Keep this ASC 606 product guide separate from the existing revenue-data-model guide: the latter's statement that it names no governing standard remains accurate for that source.
Do not elevate Metronome's data and reporting claims into accounting correctness, export completeness, close-control, or auditor-approval guarantees.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]] - ASC 606 five-step product mapping, reporting and reconciliation inputs, timing tensions, worked-detail route, and accounting-authority boundary

For ASC 606-oriented reporting, Metronome's guide treats persistent contract identity, dates, amendments, version history, related-agreement linkage, and CRM or ERP identifiers as inputs to the customer's contract assessment. Usage, charges, and credits should retain contract attribution, but Metronome does not determine whether agreements must be combined, whether a modification is prospective or retrospective, the enforceable period under an opt-out, or the accounting treatment of free periods. Those decisions remain customer-owned accounting conclusions. [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]]
warnings: The guide describes linkage and version-history support at a high level; use dedicated contract and edit-history sources for actual schemas, coverage, retention, and behavior.
Do not equate Metronome customer account hierarchy with an accounting conclusion that several legal agreements form one ASC 606 contract.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]] - contract identity, amendment and linkage inputs for ASC 606 workflows, with customer-owned combination, modification, enforceable-period, and policy decisions

Metronome's ASC 606 guide uses product and rate-card structures, tags or custom fields, charge-level reporting, consistent identifiers, historical raw amounts, and pricing or discount detail as inputs for obligation mapping, standalone-selling-price analysis, and downstream allocation. A SKU is not automatically a distinct performance obligation: the customer owns that determination and the mapping. Metronome supplies granular data but does not perform SSP allocation or reallocation and does not establish variable-consideration, foreign-exchange, material-right, or other accounting policy. [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]]
warnings: Keep product identifiers and tags as data-model inputs rather than accounting determinations.
Do not treat the worked SKU, bundle, discount, or SSP examples as prescriptive policy.

concepts.proposed_markdown: - [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]] - SKU and obligation mapping, pricing and discount inputs, historical SSP evidence, downstream allocation support, and accounting-decision boundary

Metronome's ASC 606 guide says recognition follows satisfaction or control transfer and warns that invoice timing and recognition often differ. Its appendix nevertheless describes on-demand and overage amounts as recognized upon invoicing and a postpaid true-up as recognized on finalization. Preserve those as illustrative reporting treatments rather than a universal trigger: invoice issuance, finalization, usage, drawdown, expiration, or true-up does not by itself prove the merchant's performance-obligation, allocation, variable-consideration, breakage, or recognition conclusion. [[source-metronome-guides-reporting-insights-financial-reporting-asc-606-revenue-recognition]]
warnings: This is a material source-internal timing tension; do not silently choose invoice timing as accounting truth.
Retain the existing source-specific invoice status mappings without promoting them to GAAP, ERP-posting, or close-control authority.

warnings: Treat every worked timing and amount as illustrative; the customer owns breakage, variable-consideration, performance-obligation, allocation, and recognition policy.
